article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-dominant hybrid
Genetics: Skunk #1 × Afghani
Breeder: Magus Genetics
THC Content: 20%
CBD Content: 1%
Terpene Profile: myrcene , pinene , beta-caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Sweet fruit, sour citrus, Skunk, herbs
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Mid to late October
Indoor Yield: 400–500 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: Moderate
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Warlock is a useful reminder that an indica plant does not need to deliver an indica-style high. Developed during the formative years of Dutch cannabis breeding, this compact Afghani-and-Skunk hybrid grows with the sturdy architecture and thick flower production expected from indica-dominant marijuana, yet its effect can be strikingly cerebral. Sweet fruit and sour notes rise from the buds above Skunk, herbs, and earth, while relatively little leaf surrounds the large flower clusters—a trait that made the cultivar popular with growers long before modern “bag appeal” became a standard selling point.

Warlock began as the flagship creation of Magus Genetics and eventually became part of Serious Seeds when the two breeding programs joined forces. Serious Seeds now preserves both regular and feminized versions and lists approximately 20% THC, 1% CBD, an eight-to-nine-week flowering cycle, and indoor yields around 400–500 grams per square meter.
Genetics and Lineage

Warlock is fundamentally a Skunk × Afghani hybrid. Serious Seeds describes the parents as a well-known Skunk and an Afghan strain, while historical Magus Genetics material more specifically identifies the combination as Skunk #1 × Afghani. The genetic work was conducted by Gerrit of Magus Genetics, who spent years working through dozens of breeding lines before selecting the combination that became Warlock. Serious Seeds’ historical account notes that he worked with roughly 50 breeding lines derived from 25 females and two males while developing the cultivar.

The parents contribute complementary characteristics. Afghani genetics provide compact stature, resin production, physical sturdiness, and dense flower formation. Skunk brings stronger branching, pungent aromatics, hybrid vigor, and the more energetic cerebral character that separates Warlock from a conventional Afghan indica. The finished plant remains predominantly indica, but it stretches noticeably after flowering begins and develops an unusually high calyx-to-leaf ratio. Those sativa-like characteristics are exactly why the strain can look like a stocky indica during vegetative growth yet produce a head-focused effect after harvest.

Warlock eventually became much more than an isolated cultivar. After Magus Genetics closed, Serious Seeds incorporated the genetic line into its collection in 2012. The strain had already been used to create several notable descendants, including Double Dutch , where Warlock was crossed with Serious Seeds’ Chronic , as well as Exile and other Magus projects. Serious Seeds continues to describe Warlock as the genetic “stallion” behind a significant portion of the old Magus catalog.
Effects and Experience

Warlock’s most distinctive characteristic is the disconnect between plant structure and psychoactive character. Although predominantly indica, the high tends to arrive mentally rather than physically. The opening can feel alert, focused, euphoric, and creatively engaging. Music, conversation, reading, art, or thoughtful solitary activities may become more absorbing without the immediate heaviness associated with classic Afghan weed. Serious Seeds specifically characterizes the effect as strong, active, and more cerebral than physical.

Physical relaxation gradually appears beneath the head high, but it generally does not erase the mentally engaged quality at moderate doses. This makes Warlock unusually versatile for an indica-dominant cultivar. An experienced consumer may find it appropriate for an afternoon or early evening when relaxation is desirable but complete sedation is not. Higher doses can produce considerably more physical weight, especially once the initial mental stimulation has settled.

Serious Seeds currently gives the cultivar an approximate cannabinoid profile of 20% THC and 1% CBD. Those figures are moderate compared with modern flower marketed above 30% THC, but Warlock should not automatically be considered mild. Its reputation was established largely through the subjective strength and duration of its high rather than headline laboratory numbers. Consumers with limited tolerance may still encounter dry mouth, dizziness, increased anxiety, or impaired concentration when too much is consumed.
Medical Benefits

Warlock has a long history within medical cannabis communities because its cerebral effect can remain relatively active while the body becomes more relaxed. Some medical marijuana consumers may find that combination useful when they want temporary relief from everyday tension without immediately becoming sleepy. The cultivar’s mentally focused quality may also appeal to people who dislike extremely heavy marijuana strains during the earlier part of the day.

Its historical medical reputation became significant enough that Serious Seeds later collaborated with Canada’s House of the Great Gardener to produce CBD Warlock by crossing the original cultivar with Cannatonic. The breeder reports that this separate CBD-oriented hybrid produced substantially higher cannabidiol levels than the original, including plants with roughly balanced THC and CBD profiles. That project should not be confused with ordinary Warlock, which Serious Seeds currently lists at roughly 20% THC and 1% CBD.

Neither Warlock nor CBD Warlock should be treated as proof that a particular cannabis cultivar treats a specific illness. Effects vary with dosage, cannabinoid chemistry, individual physiology, medications, tolerance, and consumption method. Anyone using marijuana for medical purposes should place greater weight on the laboratory analysis of the actual product and professional healthcare guidance than on a strain’s historical reputation.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Warlock’s aroma is considerably fruitier than its Skunk-and-Afghani pedigree might initially imply. Serious Seeds describes the bouquet as strong and sweet with an acidic edge resembling fresh fruit. The sweetness can suggest ripe fruit or fruit candy without becoming as syrupy as modern dessert strains . Once the flowers are broken apart, more traditional cannabis aromas begin emerging: Skunk, dry herbs, earth, and mild spice.

The flavor follows a similar progression. Sweet fruit tends to lead the inhale, followed by a sharper sour or citrus-like edge. Earth, herbs, and Skunk become more obvious through the finish, creating a profile that feels noticeably different from modern Gelato- or Runtz-derived marijuana. The breeder also notes that individual plants can express several terpene profiles, including more bitter variations, so some phenotypes may lean considerably less sweet than others.

No standardized breeder terpene laboratory panel is published for the original Warlock. Modern descriptions often associate the cultivar with myrcene, pinene, and beta-caryophyllene, but precise terpene dominance should be considered batch-specific rather than a permanent genetic specification. This is an older cannabis line developed before terpene percentages became a routine part of seed-bank marketing.
Growing Information

Warlock was selected with practical cultivation in mind. During vegetative growth, plants remain relatively short and thick, making the strain suitable for rooms where vertical space is limited. Once flowering begins, however, the stems stretch and produce large, compact flower clusters. Serious Seeds recommends approximately three to five weeks of vegetative growth followed by eight to nine weeks of flowering. The breeder gives a typical flowering time of about 60 days.

One of the cultivar’s most useful traits is its unusually low leaf-to-flower ratio. Mature buds contain relatively few small leaves, making trimming considerably easier than with many bushier indica varieties. White pistils gradually turn tan or dark pink as the flowers approach maturity, providing another visual indication that harvest is approaching. Indoor yield is officially listed at approximately 400–500 g/m².

The flowering stretch should still be planned for. Plants that appear compact before the light cycle changes can elongate substantially afterward, so topping, gentle low-stress training, or a broad canopy can make more efficient use of available space. Outdoors, Serious Seeds places harvest around mid-to-late October. The combination of strong branching and dense flower production makes airflow important during the final weeks, particularly in climates where cool autumn nights bring elevated humidity.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Warlock?

Warlock is a Skunk × Afghani hybrid originally bred by Magus Genetics. Historical Magus material identifies the lineage more specifically as Skunk #1 × Afghani. Serious Seeds now preserves and sells the cultivar after incorporating the former Magus Genetics lines into its breeding program.
Is Warlock indica or sativa?

Warlock is predominantly indica, but several characteristics are surprisingly sativa-like. It stretches during flowering and produces a strong cerebral, active high rather than immediately creating a heavy body stone.
How strong is the Warlock strain?

Serious Seeds currently lists approximately 20% THC and 1% CBD. The breeder characterizes the psychoactive effect as very strong and primarily cerebral. Actual cannabinoid concentration can vary with phenotype and cultivation.
What does Warlock taste like?

Sweet and slightly sour fresh fruit forms the main profile, accompanied by Skunk, herbs, earth, and subtle spice. Individual phenotypes can range from sweeter fruit expressions to more bitter and pungent variations.
How long does Warlock take to flower?

Serious Seeds lists an eight-to-nine-week indoor flowering period, with approximately 60 days being typical. Outdoor plants generally finish around mid-to-late October in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates.
Final Thoughts on Warlock

Warlock earned classic status without relying on exotic parent names or extreme THC claims. Gerrit of Magus Genetics used ordinary but carefully selected Afghani and Skunk material, worked through numerous breeding lines, and produced a cultivar sufficiently distinctive to become the flagship of the entire seed company. Serious Seeds later preserved the line when Magus Genetics closed, allowing Warlock to remain commercially available decades after its original development.

Its staying power comes from an unusual combination of traits. Plants remain manageable, flower in roughly eight to nine weeks, yield around 400–500 g/m² indoors, produce enormous buds with little leaf, and finish with an active cerebral high that contrasts sharply with their indica-dominant genetics. Sweet-and-sour fruit over Skunk and earth provides an equally recognizable old-school flavor. For cannabis enthusiasts interested in influential European genetics from before the dominance of Cookies, Gelato, and Runtz, Warlock remains an important example of how careful selection can turn two familiar genetic families into marijuana with a personality entirely its own.
